advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass an explicit `timeout=` to `urllib.request.urlopen` in `_download()` so scanner fetches fail fast rather than hang the build.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:237 `with urllib.request.urlopen(url) as response, dest.open("wb") as fh:` — no `timeout=` argument
`search_files` for `timeout` in `scripts/install_review_scanners.py` returned `(no matches)`
Called from `_install_gitleaks` at line 315 `_download(entry.gitleaks_url, archive)` inside the Docker build RUN (Dockerfile.reviewbot:52)
advisory.finding: `_download()` in `scripts/install_review_scanners.py` calls `urllib.request.urlopen(url)` with no timeout, so a stalled connection to the Gitleaks release URL blocks indefinitely. This runs both inside the Docker build (`RUN ... install --platform linux/arm64`) and in `make scanner-integration`, so a hung upstream fetch has no cap of its own and relies entirely on an outer job/build timeout that the new workflow does not set.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either verify the Gitleaks archive digest against the fetched `checksums_url` asset at install/validate time, or drop the `checksums_url` field and the provenance claim in docs so the manifest is not misrepresented as provenance-checked.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:44 `gitleaks_checksums_url: str` and :127 `gitleaks_checksums_url=str(gitleaks["checksums_url"])` — parsed and stored
`search_files` for `checksums_url` returned only the dataclass field, the required-keys set (:106), and the assignment (:127) — no fetch/compare use
scripts/install_review_scanners.py:318 `_verify_digest(archive, entry.gitleaks_sha256)` — archive verified only against the manifest's own sha256
docs/security.md added text: 'checksum provenance: the Gitleaks release `*_checksums.txt` URL used at lock-update time' — implies provenance verification that code does not perform
advisory.finding: The lock manifest declares a `checksums_url` per platform and it is carried onto `PlatformEntry.gitleaks_checksums_url`, but the installer never fetches or verifies against that upstream `*_checksums.txt`. `_verify_digest` compares the downloaded archive only to the manifest's own `sha256` field, so the 'checksum provenance' that docs/security.md promises is documentation-only, not enforced. A wrong/tampered `sha256` committed to the manifest would be trusted as-is.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests driving validate_manifest()/main(['validate-locks']) with (a) divergent per-platform semgrep versions and (b) a manifest version not matching its requirements lock, asserting ScannerInstallError / non-zero exit.
evidence: scripts/install_review_scanners.py:208-212 raises `f"{selected}: manifest Semgrep {entry.semgrep_version} does not match {entry.semgrep_requirements.name}"` — an added contract
scripts/install_review_scanners.py:214-215 `if len(versions) != 1: raise ScannerInstallError("all platform locks must use the same top-level Semgrep version")` — an added contract
.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml:67 `python scripts/install_review_scanners.py validate-locks` runs this as the CI pre-gate

In test_code_review_ws5.py every reference to validate_manifest monkeypatches it away: lines 779, 816, 845 `monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "validate_manifest", lambda _manifest: None)`; test_review_scanner_lock_manifest_has_two_platform_contracts (line 654) reads the manifest directly but never calls validate_manifest or main(['validate-locks'])

Named violating inputs with no test: (a) a manifest whose linux/amd64 semgrep.version is 1.145.0 while linux/arm64 is 1.146.0 must raise 'all platform locks must use the same top-level Semgrep version'; (b) a manifest whose semgrep.version is 1.145.0 while the requirements lock pins semgrep==1.146.0 must raise the 'does not match' error
advisory.finding: The newly-added manifest-consistency contract in validate_manifest() (and the 'validate-locks' CLI mode that CI runs as its pre-gate) is untested: neither the manifest-Semgrep-version-vs-requirements-lock mismatch branch nor the cross-platform top-level-version divergence branch is exercised.
scenarios: A future scanner bump edits one platform's requirements lock but leaves the manifest version or the other platform stale — validate-locks should fail-closed but the branch has no regression test
A silent divergence between the amd64 and arm64 Semgrep pins passes review because nothing exercises the divergence guard
advisory.suggested_fix: Add two tests using a tmp manifest + --manifest/--lock: one where the two platform entries pin different top-level semgrep versions (expect 'all platform locks must use the same top-level Semgrep version'), and one where manifest semgrep.version disagrees with the lock's semgrep== pin (expect the 'does not match' error); also assert main(['validate-locks', '--manifest', <good>]) returns 0 and prints 'review scanner locks: OK'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the scanner lane does not silently pass (exit 0) when install_review_scanners.py is missing on a change that is expected to have it.
evidence: if [ ! -f scripts/install_review_scanners.py ]; then
echo "scripts/install_review_scanners.py not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping"
exit 0
python scripts/install_review_scanners.py validate-locks
advisory.finding: The scanner-integration reusable workflow silently exits 0 when scripts/install_review_scanners.py is absent, meaning the hash-lock validation (validate-locks) can be skipped without failing the lane.
scenarios: A patchset that removes or renames install_review_scanners.py bypasses lock validation entirely while the lane reports green.

evidence: gerrit-verify.yaml:518 `) && env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION || 'failure' }}` — the whole per-route success gate is ANDed with the run-wide aggregate conclusion
gerrit-verify.yaml:460 `uses: im-open/workflow-conclusion@...` aggregates the run's job conclusions (all jobs, not the vote job's `needs`)
gerrit-verify.yaml:456 vote `needs:` list omits `scanner-integration`, so FAILURE_OBSERVED/CONCLUSION per-job checks don't cover it — but WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION still does
gerrit-verify.yaml:255 comment: 'the Verified vote does not wait for or normalize over its result'
scripts/normalize_ci_conclusion.py:25 `if conclusion == "failure": return "failure"` — a 'failure' aggregate maps straight to a -1 vote
advisory.finding: The advisory scanner-integration lane can taint the Verified vote: the vote job's CONCLUSION expression gates on `env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION`, which `im-open/workflow-conclusion` derives from ALL jobs in the run (including scanner-integration), so a failing advisory scanner lane forces CONCLUSION='failure' -> Verified -1, despite ADR-0114 stating the Verified vote 'does not wait for or normalize over its result.'
advisory.suggested_fix: Stop deriving CONCLUSION from the run-wide `im-open/workflow-conclusion` aggregate; compute the vote conclusion solely from the explicit per-route `needs.*.result` checks already present in the CONCLUSION expression (drop the `&& env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION`), so only jobs in the vote's `needs` list can affect the vote.

dropped.finding: The new reusable workflow `.github/workflows/_scanner-integration.yml` sets no `timeout-minutes` on its `scanner-integration` job, unlike sibling reusables (e.g. `_build-and-test.yml` sets 30/60). It installs native scanners over the network and runs pytest; a hung download or test lets the job run to GitHub's 6-hour default, wasting a runner and (in the advisory Gerrit lane) leaving the patchset check pending indefinitely.
dropped.suggested_fix: Add `timeout-minutes: 15` (cold cost is documented as 1.5–3 min) under the `scanner-integration:` job.
